reviews.text: The deputy director is the worst. I was under his care for the last few years. On the last day, I went straight there from the emergency hospital. When I told him that data had been sent from the emergency hospital, the deputy director said, "I can't receive it, so I'll look at it later." I left my dog ​​there, and that was the last time I saw my beloved dog alive. Did he look at it right away? Did he even look at it at all? What did it say? If he had looked at it right away, I might have been able to be by my dog's side at the end. Even if I couldn't be there at the end, if I had thought it through and made the choice myself, I might not have regretted it so much. I wish they would handle things more properly for the sake of pet owners. I wish the doctor at that time had been the director. No matter how much I regret it, I pray that something unfortunate happens to the deputy director as well.

Both the head veterinarian and the deputy head veterinarian provided attentive care, and I felt confident in their medical skills. I am truly grateful for their unwavering dedication until the very end.

The veteran nurse, who has been there for a long time, may seem unfriendly at first glance, but her responses are precise and she is a very kind person.

On the other hand, I was a little disappointed with the reception staff's attitude. Even when my pet was on the verge of death and immediately afterward, they remained purely businesslike and did not show any empathy, which left me feeling somewhat sad. It's such a good hospital, but the reception staff's attitude was a bit disappointing and still remains in my memory.
The doctor is very skilled, cheerful, and kind. Both the head doctor and the deputy head doctor are young, so I feel confident continuing my visits here. It's best to make a reservation by phone.

Pet hotel rabbits are also available.

Basically, it's for dogs and cats.

It's a hospital, so it's fine if anything happens, but I'm a little worried because they specialize in dogs and cats.

I'll be staying there with food, supplements, and enough Timothy hay for the necessary days. It's cheap, but I can't check their daily routine or whether they move around in the room properly.

It's a hospital, not a hotel.

Apparently, they'll be sharing a room with the cats, but I wonder what it's like for rabbits? Each one is different, but mine is shy and doesn't know other animals, so it might have been scary.

It's a hospital after all, so it mainly caters to dogs and cats, so small animals like rabbits might be out of place?
My diarrhea, which hadn't been cured after visiting three different hospitals, was cured by the doctor's prescription. It's amazing. It was worth the effort of taking the train and bus to get there.
The teachers are friendly and give thorough explanations. I still drive there even though I've moved.

This is Shimise from the animal hospital. My family's pets have been under your care for over 30 years. It's a hospital where you can leave your pets with peace of mind. My current pet is my third, and I hope you'll continue to take care of us in the future. I don't want to be separated from them just yet.
